newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold imports up 4.87 pct in first 10 months.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold imports up 4.87 pct in first 10 months.

text.p: Gold imports into Dubai, a major trading centre for the precious metal, rose 4.87 per cent to 283.01 tonnes in the first 10 months of 1996 from 269.86 tonnes in the same period last year, the World Gold Council (WGC) said.
In October alone, imports increased by 13.74 per cent to 28.41 tonnes from 24.98 tonnes in October 1995, mainly because of demand ahead of the Hindu festival of lights, Diwali.

WGC Middle East and India chief executive Rolf Schneebeli said in a statement new gold designs and products developed over the past year helped in attracting more buyers from India and the Middle East.
"Dubai is also on track to achieve higher gold imports than last year on a year-to-year comparison," he added.

"Local demand has risen, as has demand from the subcontinent and neighbouring markets like Iran. This is only a reinforcement of the statement that Dubai is indeed the true city of gold," Schneebli said.
In the first 10 months of the year Dubai imported gold from 27 countries, with most coming from Switzerland, Britain and South Africa.
The Geneva-based WGC is a non-profit association owned by major gold producers and monitors about 75 percent of the world's markets.
